newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen shoot to new highs in bullish trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen shoot to new highs in bullish trade.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures bounded to new contract highs on Thursday on the back of a rally in U.S. bond markets and buying of short-term cash Japanese government bonds (JGBs).

"I thought it would be quiet today ahead of the U.S. non-farm payrolls report (on Friday)," said a dealer with a U.S. institution, adding that a fall in the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) rate also boosted sentiment.

"People are not expecting any rate hike in the U.S. so they won't do anything in Japan either," he said, adding that March Euroyen was likely to target 99.36 of it cleared through resistance at 99.30/31.
The contract finished at 99.30 after hitting a high of 99.31 against its IMM close at 99.24. December and June reached contract highs of 99.43 and 99.16 respectively.
"Sentiment is still strong. The 3-month CD rate fell to 0.52 percent for the first time since December 1995," said a dealer with a European futures house.
"As long as the JGBs continue to pick up, the market should still go higher," he said, adding that December JGB futures faced resistance near 122.70.
They settled at 122.61 against their opening 122.11 after attempting a new high at 122.66.

Eurodollar futures finished on firm ground following an overnight rally in U.S. treasuries on growing expectations that the volatile non-farm payrolls report would show a slowdown in U.S. jobs growth in September.

The dealer at the U.S. institution said the market was likely to consolidate its gains ahead of the figure on Friday, and the December and March contracts facing resistance at 94.32 and 94.25 respectively.
They ended scarcely changed from their IMM settlements at 94.30 and 94.20 respectively.
